I verified both R2 hashes (`bc72fa30…519`, `50fcff45…903`), the incorporated immutable R1 by hash, base HEAD `9c4dce4547781293b5cd089f018a63aedad75428`, and all ten compiler-source hashes byte-for-byte at that head. I then re-derived the security architecture from the full current `static_compile`, `layout`, `relation` (mod and compiler), `local_deployment`, `custody`, `prepare`, `signed`, `proving::source_closure`, and CLI `compile_call` production paths rather than relying on diff claims: the native single-owner custody guard remains intact, the unsigned emitter constrains only token/recipient/amount, and every native and signed consumer recompiles strictly before any decode, VM, `k`, key, or proof work.

All six R1 clarifications are resolved: the explicit mapped-roles CLI shape with mode-derived export and inspect qualifications, consumer and README migration, and the retained legacy unsigned negative; the from-only deduplicated, sorted, always-serialized `debit_sources` with the exact asset, debit-role, then recipient-role error order; `compiler_hash` as exactly the pure `proving::source_closure()`; the `pub(crate)` capability boundary with the length-1 custom decoder arm and named compile-fail locations and no conversion bridge to native artifacts, seeds, or proving capability; the coherent single-payer-derived fixtures proving exact `one-public-payer` refusal before any native work; and the refreshed candidate identity. Three non-blocking observations (minor line-citation drift, crate-internal accessor discipline, and doctest strength) are recorded for the implementing candidate's audit.

This vote carries native authority 0 and approves no implementation or result. Root adoption is required before shared implementation, and a fresh Muse audit of the full implemented candidate and its actual QA results remains mandatory, with the full roadmap and M11 still open.
